problems.title: The public entry point omits object-specific latent blending
problems.source_location: Algorithm 1, PDF p.7; app.py generate_image; pipeline_scenedesigner.py denoising loop
claim: The paper sets \(z_0=x_t+\Delta t\,v_g\), forms each \(u_i=x_t+\Delta t\,v_i\), and replaces masked regions by \(z_i=(1-M_i)\odot z_{i-1}+M_i\odot u_i\).
analysis: The application passes only global condition/prompt data and the denoising path advances a single global prediction; renderer-created individual object files are not consumed by that call. With a \(2\times2\) zero latent, \(\Delta t=1/2\), global velocity \(1\), object velocity \(2\), and a mask selecting one pixel, global-only output is \(0.5\) everywhere, while Algorithm 1 gives \(1\) at the selected pixel. Their difference is exactly \(M_1\Delta t(v_1-v_g)\); empty masks or equal velocities are agreement cases.
result: The released entry point does not reproduce DOS. This does not prove the historical experiments omitted it or that DOS cannot improve outputs.
repair: The published ordered mask recurrence is the verified local update. An integrated implementation additionally needs object prompts, maps, latent masks and matching scheduler/overlap conventions; no complete pipeline repair is claimed.
problems.existing_correction_status: The public report in repository issue 3, dated 28 February 2026, had already raised this release gap. No accepted integrated correction is established.
problems.impact_rationale: This is a local implementation or interpretation defect; damage to the central empirical result has not been established.
